items.q: In the 'Other Properties' table, the specific gravity printed for BLOOD is:
items.exp: The table pairs urine 1.020–1.040 with blood 1.010; 1.005 is the diabetes-insipidus cut-off in the abnormal-values table below. (Book p741)

items.q: Fill up: The normal urine pH printed in this table is ______, described as acidic.
items.exp: Row 1: pH — urine 4–4.5 (Acidic) against blood 7.35–7.40. (Book p741)

items.q: In the acidification diagram, K+ is drawn entering the α-intercalated cell at the luminal membrane while H+ leaves through the H+ ATPase.
opts: True — the two arrows at the luminal membrane point in opposite directions
False — K+ is shown leaving the cell into the lumen
False — no potassium arrow appears anywhere in the diagram
True — but the H+ arrow points into the cell, not out
items.exp: The figure labels the luminal membrane H+ ATPase with H+ exiting, a second ATPase with K+ entering, and the boxed cell as the α-intercalated cell of the cortical collecting duct (CCD). (Book p741)

items.q: Urinary concentration on this page is credited to all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: ADH secreted from the posterior pituitary
A medullary interstitium whose osmolality is raised by urea
items.exp: The three bullets under 'Concentration' are ADH → free water reabsorption, medullary interstitium ↑ osmolality d/t urea, and vasa recta; aldosterone is not listed. (Book p741)

items.q: A patient with 4 L/day of dilute urine has urine osmolality 250 mOsm/kg and specific gravity 1.003, with a normal serum creatinine. Which row of the abnormal-values table does this match?
opts: Diabetes insipidus — specific gravity <1.005 and osmolality <300 mOsm/kg
Isosthenuria — urinary parameters equal to blood parameters
Type-1 RTA — urine pH above 5.5 for 3 days
Normal concentration, since both values are simply dilute
items.exp: The table flags diabetes insipidus (↑ dilute urine) when urine specific gravity falls below 1.005 and osmolality below 300 mOsm/kg; isosthenuria instead equals blood parameters and points to ATN/CTID. (Book p741)
